done.why: I dropped the grue repellent can into the lake and could not pick it up again. The dark passage south of the lake looked like the way on, and I didn't think I could cross it without the can.

about: An underground dungeon that starts at the foot of a stair. You fight a hooded double of yourself, explore a shadowy land, and cross a freezing lake. Past the lake is a grue-infested dark passage. A repellent can is the key to it, and a table that teleports you fetches the can.

moments.note: The sword pulled from the rock appeared in my hand for the fight with the hooded figure.
The hooded figure wore my own face. Removing its hood ended the fight.
The scenic table showed the repellent room, and touching it teleported me there.
The repellent smell faded before I could get through the dark. I was eaten.
Entering the lake with the can in my hands lost it permanently, and I couldn't recover it underwater.

wished: Know in advance how long the repellent lasts.
Pick things up from the lake bottom.
Find what shakes the cracked rock by the iron door.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face
lines.why: The best beat in the game: the fight resolves as a choice, not a kill.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you
lines.why: It states the rule about the lake in the same breath as the hazard.

fun.why: Good puzzles, but I lost progress to an unclear rule about the lake and the repellent.

engagement.why: There was always a clear next goal.

difficulty.why: The repellent timing is tight, and the lake rule can lock you out of progress.

interestingness.why: The double, the lake and the teleport table were all inventive.

prose.why: The prose is vivid and the hints are woven into it.
